usage: Used to describe a plant, person, or living thing that is in good physical condition; for plants, it often means strong, not sick, and growing well.
Commonly placed before a noun, as in 健康的... in written Chinese; in spoken Cantonese, people often use it more flexibly as a descriptive word.
You can use it in gardening talk to describe leaves, stems, or overall plant condition after watering, sunlight, or care.
Register is neutral and very common; it is a basic everyday word for learners, and it works in both general conversation and simple garden descriptions.
